subtopic: GEMM epilogue fusion / Bias + activation + norm
learningObjective: Reason about which operations can be fused as a GEMM epilogue and what the HBM-traffic benefit is.
stem: A GEMM Y = X @ W is followed by (i) bias add, (ii) elementwise activation (GELU), (iii) RMSNorm along the last axis. Select all statements about fusing these into a GEMM epilogue that are correct. (Choose all that apply.)
codeSnippet:
# Sequence to fuse:
# Y0 = X @ W                              # GEMM
# Y1 = Y0 + bias                          # (i) bias add, per-row broadcast
# Y2 = gelu(Y1)                           # (ii) elementwise activation
# Y3 = rmsnorm(Y2, gamma)                 # (iii) reduction across last axis + normalize

options.text: Fusing the epilogue removes tensor-core benefit because tensor cores can only accumulate into registers, and any epilogue instruction moves the accumulator to shared memory first, forcing a synchronous barrier that undoes the tensor-core throughput advantage.

(i) bias add and (ii) elementwise activation fuse naturally as a GEMM epilogue because they are pure elementwise transforms on the accumulator tile before it is written to HBM; the fused kernel avoids the intermediate Y0 and Y1 HBM roundtrips.

(iii) RMSNorm fuses as a standard GEMM epilogue in the same way as bias-add and activation, because normalization is elementwise once the running variance is precomputed as a scalar constant of the workload.

(iii) RMSNorm requires a reduction along the last axis (i.e., across the D_out output columns of the GEMM tile), which typically cuts across CTAs unless the GEMM is designed with a full-row tile; in mainstream libraries, RMSNorm is left as a separate kernel or fused only with a specialized 'GEMM-with-row-reduction' epilogue.

explanation: A is correct: bias add and elementwise activation are the canonical GEMM epilogue candidates. They act on the accumulator tile in registers before write-back, saving one HBM roundtrip per intermediate. C is correct: RMSNorm needs a reduction along D_out, which requires the full row to be in one CTA's tile; this constraint is rarely met by typical GEMM tile designs, so mainstream libraries either keep RMSNorm as a separate kernel or provide a dedicated GEMM+row-reduce epilogue. B is wrong: RMSNorm is not scalar-elementwise; it depends on per-row statistics. D is wrong: tensor-core epilogues run in registers/SMEM without breaking throughput.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: tensor-core epilogues are supported natively; they do not disable the tensor cores.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: RMSNorm is per-row, not element-independent.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: RMSNorm needs row-reduction which conflicts with typical GEMM tile decomposition.

assumptions: Standard cuBLASLt / CUTLASS epilogue programming model applies.
GEMM tile size does not span the full D_out row of the output.
nonImplications: Does not imply RMSNorm can never be fused with GEMM; specialized implementations exist.
Does not imply that the bias-add saves compute; it only saves an HBM roundtrip.

performanceClaim.scope: GEMM epilogue fusion candidates on tensor-core GPUs
